rule: Every sellable claim must map to a working control, export, /api/houseops endpoint, or FS27/SkyePay runtime boundary. If a capability requires deployed FS27 environment variables or database state, the UI must say so.

claims.proof: Task form and New Task button write to the browser working state; /api/houseops/tasks persists task records in the gated Worker runtime.
Vendor form writes name, request, value, contact, and status; /api/houseops/vendors persists vendor records in the gated Worker runtime.

claims.claim: Move work through open, queued, review, and done states.
claims.proof: Advance buttons update task/vendor status; /api/houseops/tasks/:id/advance and /api/houseops/vendors/:id/advance expose the cloud-backed state movement.
Blocked, review, and high-priority tasks render in Alerts and Resolve marks them done; /api/houseops/alerts/:id/resolve persists the cloud-backed resolution.
Save Proof writes a proof row with current counts; /api/houseops/proof persists proof snapshots in the gated Worker runtime.

claims.claim: Queue and export FS27 mirror packets.
claims.proof: Queue Gate Mirror writes packets; /api/houseops/gate-packets stores cloud mirror packets and export downloads houseoperations-gate-mirror-packet.json.

claims.claim: Open a local encrypted TOTP vault.
claims.proof: SkyeBox uses WebCrypto vault encryption, saves a TOTP account, displays codes, and exports encrypted backups.

claims.claim: Hand off to FS27 Gate ID, PIN, and one-time recovery code flow.
claims.proof: FS27 includes PIN setup/login/recovery/rotation functions, redirects, and PIN Gate UI; execution requires FS27 runtime database and email webhook environment.

claims.claim: Create an approved 0S plan intent or quote-only review route.
claims.proof: Billing page records bundled 0S plan scope, current setup/monthly price, quote-only standalone boundary, approved checkout or pricing-router URL, and activation boundary without pretending payment happened.
Tutorial buttons call the same app functions used by dashboard, billing, proof, and Gate-packet flows.
